scores.evidence: Phase 1: Foundation & Architecture ... Phase 2: Core CI/CD Pipeline ... Phase 3: Deployment & Release
scores.rationale: Broad substrate-to-upward ordering exists (infra, pipeline, deploy), but nothing is gated on proof and observability/security come after dependents.
No thin end-to-end production path in Phase 0; the first 10 weeks are architecture and setup, and the pilot comes only after templates are built.

scores.evidence: CI/CD orchestrator (Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, ArgoCD)
scores.rationale: Options are listed without defaults or flip conditions; irreversible decisions are not flagged.
Pilot on low-risk services and batched rollout show some risk ordering, but no widest-impact-first ordering within phases.
Security appears in Phase 1–3 (scanning, secrets) but hardening is deferred to the end and it is not treated concretely in every phase.
Observability is deferred to week 17, long after the first builds and deployments, so it is not present from day zero.
Versioning, templates and config management are mentioned, but reproducibility is not threaded through all phases.

scores.evidence: Blue-green or canary deployment patterns; Rollback procedures
scores.rationale: Rollback appears in Phase 3 and DR in Phase 7, but resilience is not present in the earliest phases.
The plan never addresses whether an AI layer applies, so it does not declare N/A.
Later phases are scheduled, but nothing is explicitly deferred with a pull-forward condition.

note: Generic waterfall-style phase list with no walking skeleton, no decision gates, and observability deferred to week 17; only loose dependency ordering and partial security and resilience coverage.
